text:
kevin: Hi team — customer on a private VPC install reports inference init failing with 502s and auth hooks timing out after we switched them to their corp proxy. They say model pulls and telemetry both fail. Can we confirm minimal egress checklist?
maria: ping — can you paste the exact error from the agent? 502 from gateway or TLS handshake errors?
kevin: gateway logs show `upstream timed out (110)` for registry calls. Agent logs also show `x509: certificate signed by unknown authority` intermittently. No packet captures yet.
alex: sounds like two issues: (1) TLS interception / missing root CA and (2) outbound allowlist blocking some hosts. Ask customer to run curl + traceroute to verify.
kevin: sent curl output: ```
curl -v https://registry.redwood-inference.com/v1/models
* Rebuilt URL to: https://registry.redwood-inference.com/v1/models
* Connected to registry.redwood-inference.com (10.1.2.3) port 443 (#0)
* TLS handshake error: Unknown CA
``` 
kevin: traceroute shows traffic going through corp proxy at 10.0.0.1 then timing out.
maria: ok. Actions:
- Confirm that TLS MITM / SSL inspection is disabled for our domains or that customer's proxy injects a CA signed by their org and that CA is trusted by the host's OS/container.
- Ensure outbound allowlist includes FQDNs below (prefer FQDN over IPs; cloud infra uses ephemeral ranges).

maria: Minimal egress list (recommended):
- registry.redwood-inference.com (443)  # model downloads and metadata
- auth.redwood-inference.com (443)      # token OIDC / long-lived refresh
- telemetry.redwood-inference.com (443) # metrics/usage
- updates.redwood-inference.com (443)   # agent updates
- models-us-west-1.redwood-inference.net (443) # region-specific model storage
- s3.amazonaws.com, *.s3.amazonaws.com (443)   # model artifacts hosted in S3
- storage.googleapis.com (443)
- pypi.org, files.pythonhosted.org (443) # python deps
- deb.debian.org, archives.ubuntu.com, security.ubuntu.com (80/443) # apt
- quay.io, ghcr.io, docker.pkg.github.com, gcr.io (443) # container images
- ocsp.digicert.com, crl3.digicert.com (80/443) # OCSP/CRL for cert validation
- time.cloudflare.com or ntp pool (123) # time sync important for TLS

alex: also note: many of our endpoints use CloudFront / Fastly or LB frontends. If they must allow by IP, include current AWS CloudFront and GCP LB ranges — but we strongly recommend FQDN/SNI allowlist. Avoid hardcoding regional IPs unless they have an auto-update mechanism.
tara: if their proxy is doing SNI inspection, the agent may fall back to IP address in TLS and break hostname validation. Ask them to configure proxy to do TLS passthrough for these hosts, or install their proxy CA into the container/system trust store.
kevin: customer is on Ubuntu 22.04 server. What exact checks should they run? I sent them these commands:
```
# test registry TLS
curl -v --resolve registry.redwood-inference.com:443:10.1.2.3 https://registry.redwood-inference.com/v1/health
# traceroute
traceroute -n registry.redwood-inference.com
# tcpdump TLS ClientHello (run on host)
sudo tcpdump -i eth0 -s 0 -w /tmp/trace.pcap 'tcp port 443'
# check cert chain
openssl s_client -connect registry.redwood-inference.com:443 -servername registry.redwood-inference.com -showcerts
```
maria: good. Also capture `strace` of the agent process if you hit unknown CA errors to show which cert store it's loading. For containerized installs, ensure `/etc/ssl/certs` and update-ca-certificates includes the proxy CA.
alex: quick firewall example rule (iptables nftables/cloud): allow outbound TLS to FQDN via proxy bypass or allow direct 443:
```
# example (host firewall): allow direct to registry
iptables -A OUTPUT -p tcp -d registry.redwood-inference.com --dport 443 -j ACCEPT
# if using proxy, allow CONNECT to proxy for these hosts
iptables -A OUTPUT -p tcp --dport 3128 -d 10.0.0.1 -j ACCEPT
```
kevin: customer reports they have a corporate SSL inspection appliance. They asked whether we can support intercepted TLS if they present a custom CA.
maria: we can support it IF the CA is installed into the host/container trust store and the proxy does not rewrite SNI or alter Host headers. Important constraints:
- Agent validates hostname in TLS. If proxy terminates TLS and re-initiates with a different CN/subjectAltName, the agent will fail unless CN matches our FQDN.
- OCSP stapling and CRL checks must pass. If proxy blocks OCSP endpoints we saw x509 errors.
- For audit/compliance customers we prefer a split-tunnel: allow direct outbound to our domains and route only other traffic via proxy.

alex: if they cannot bypass MITM, request these items in ticket:
- Output of `openssl s_client -connect registry.redwood-inference.com:443 -servername registry.redwood-inference.com -CApath /etc/ssl/certs`
- tcpdump pcap showing ClientHello / ServerHello
- `strace` snippet showing underlying `open()` calls for CA bundle
- proxy ACL logs showing CONNECT allowed/denied for our hosts

kevin: made a support ticket. Customer attached pcap showing proxy re-signing certs and an OCSP timeout. They plan to whitelist OCSP endpoints and add our FQDNs to the proxy passthrough list.
maria: next steps: I'll move to Tier2 and provide the KB snippet. Short KB we should give them (copyable):
```
Redwood minimal egress allowlist (recommended):
- *.redwood-inference.com (443)
- registry.redwood-inference.com
- auth.redwood-inference.com
- telemetry.redwood-inference.com
- updates.redwood-inference.com
- pypi.org, files.pythonhosted.org
- deb.debian.org, archives.ubuntu.com
- quay.io, ghcr.io, gcr.io
- s3.amazonaws.com, storage.googleapis.com
- ocsp.digicert.com, crl3.digicert.com

Proxy/TLS guidelines:
- Prefer TLS passthrough for the list above.
- If TLS interception is unavoidable, install proxy CA on the host/container and ensure SNI and Host headers are preserved.
- Allow outbound TCP 443 and TCP/80 to OCSP/CRL endpoints and package repos.
- Ensure system clock is NTP-synced.
```
kevin: customer accepted; they will add allowlist + enable OCSP endpoints. We'll retest after their change.
deploy-bot: ticket RDW-5231 updated: assigned to maria. :white_check_mark:
maria: closing loop — will follow up with a short KB entry and attach curl/traceroute snippets for future installs. :thumbsup:
